articles.headline: La ola de robos de cable de cobre paraliza aserraderos de A Mariña
articles.subtitle: Fearmaga alerta de una «ola de robos» en instalaciones de toda Galicia: dos detenidos por el golpe de Alfoz y Lourenzá y cuatro más en Lugo por sacar cobre del alcantarillado, con paradas de producción de hasta dos semanas.
articles.body:
La Federación Empresarial de Aserraderos y Rematantes de Maderas de Galicia (Fearmaga) ha alertado de una «ola de robos» de cable de cobre en instalaciones de sus asociados, después del asalto registrado el sábado por la noche en las naves de Maderas José Saiz en Alfoz y Lourenzá, que se saldó con dos detenidos que ingresaron en prisión.

La Guardia Civil localizó al menos una tonelada del cable sustraído escondida en un monte, lo que apunta a que los autores pensaban volver a recogerlo. El sector advierte de que el problema trasciende el valor del metal: sin cableado se detienen líneas de producción completas y algunas empresas han tenido que parar dos semanas o más. Fearmaga ha pedido una reunión con el delegado del Gobierno para analizar la situación.

El mismo patrón —cuadrillas que simulan trabajos de mantenimiento— aparece en la detención de cuatro personas en Lugo por la Policía Nacional. Un agente fuera de servicio observó a varias personas levantando tapas de alcantarillado y avisó; junto a una furgoneta, dos de los sospechosos dijeron primero que reparaban postes de luz y los otros dos, que salían de una alcantarilla, que atendían una avería de fibra óptica.

En el registro del vehículo aparecieron herramientas y maquinaria para cortar y extraer cableado, además de equipos de radiotransmisión. La Policía sostiene que estos grupos actúan a plena luz del día, con ropa de trabajo y elementos de señalización, y se reparten las tareas entre quienes bajan al subsuelo y quienes vigilan el entorno.

articles.headline: Lugo dona sangre y guarda silencio por las víctimas del siniestro de Urda
articles.subtitle: Vecinos llenaron el autobús de donación instalado en la Praza Maior tras el llamamiento urgente, y el Concello secundó el minuto de silencio de la FEMP con Galicia aún en duelo por Angrois.
articles.body:
Los lucenses respondieron este miércoles al llamamiento urgente de donación de sangre lanzado tras el choque de dos trenes en Urda (Toledo), que dejó al menos 68 muertos y decenas de heridos. El vehículo de la agencia gallega de donación, estacionado en la Praza Maior ante el Círculo de las Artes, recibió a vecinos durante toda la tarde.

La convocatoria no respondía a ninguna necesidad de los hospitales de Lugo, sino a la idea de reforzar las reservas ante las necesidades derivadas del siniestro. A la solidaridad ciudadana se sumó el Concello, que secundó el minuto de silencio convocado por la Federación Española de Municipios y Provincias y celebrado con el recuerdo del Alvia de Angrois, en el que murieron 80 personas.

En Lugo el acto contó con la presencia del secretario xeral del PSdeG, José Ramón Gómez Besteiro. Otros ayuntamientos gallegos repitieron la concentración, con el presidente de la Xunta, Alfonso Rueda, en la de Pontevedra. Para este jueves están previstos un homenaje en el Parlamento de Galicia, en la sede de la Xunta en San Caetano y en la Delegación del Gobierno, además de cinco minutos de silencio en las estaciones convocados por el comité de empresa de Renfe.

articles.headline: El choque de dos trenes en Urda deja al menos 68 muertos y abre una crisis política
articles.subtitle: Un AVE de Renfe y un Iryo detenido colisionaron tras una orden del centro de control de Adif para «reanudar la marcha normal»; Sánchez habla de dos siniestros «inasumibles» en un año y Feijóo exige una auditoría de la red.
articles.body:
El choque de dos trenes de alta velocidad en la estación de Urda (Toledo) ha dejado al menos 68 muertos y 107 heridos, una veintena de ellos en la UCI, según el balance de los servicios de emergencia. Es el siniestro ferroviario más grave en España desde el descarrilamiento del Alvia en Angrois, en 2013, que costó 80 vidas.

El accidente se produjo cuando un AVE de Renfe que cubría la línea Madrid-Sevilla impactó contra un Iryo que estaba detenido ante la señal de entrada a la estación. La maquinista del Iryo había advertido por radio de que no podía reiniciar el sistema LZB. Minutos después, el centro de control de Adif autorizó al AVE a seguir: «Desconecte y vuelva a conectar el LZB. Y reanude la marcha. Al amparo del BSL. Con marcha normal».

## Una orden «inexplicable»

El ministro de Transportes, Óscar Puente, calificó esa instrucción de «inexplicable» y situó la responsabilidad en el operario del centro de control, al que la Guardia Civil ya ha interrogado. La jueza ha abierto diligencias y los drones del instituto armado sobrevuelan la zona para levantar un mapa en 3D de la colisión y de los vagones.

Sánchez, que decretó tres días de duelo oficial y dejó en suspenso la precampaña del 29-N, aseguró que «no es asumible para España dos accidentes de tren en un mismo año» y prometió contundencia cuando se conozcan las causas. Feijóo reclama una revisión independiente de toda la red ferroviaria.

articles.headline: La pericia judicial tasa las joyas de Zapatero en más de un millón de euros
articles.subtitle: La Joyería Yanes cifra el lote en 1.023.000 euros y sostiene que las piezas pudieron fabricarse en India, Tailandia o China después de 2007, lo que contradice la versión del expresidente sobre un regalo saudí anterior.
articles.body:
El juez de la Audiencia Nacional José Luis Calama ya dispone del informe pericial encargado a la Joyería Yanes sobre las piezas halladas en la caja fuerte del despacho de José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero. El documento tasa el lote en 1.023.000 euros, una cifra próxima a la estimación inicial que hizo la Joyería Ansorena al comienzo de las pesquisas.

El peritaje sostiene que las joyas «pudieran haber sido fabricadas en India, Tailandia, China o países de Asia central». Los diamantes y las esmeraldas son naturales, aunque de calidad «muy comercial», y las gemas rojas no pueden denominarse rubíes porque llevan relleno de vidrio de plomo. Los zafiros podrían proceder de Tailandia.

Sobre la antigüedad, los joyeros concluyen que los tres lotes que Zapatero habría recibido como obsequio de Arabia Saudí se fabricaron simultáneamente y, por el contenido de níquel, después de junio de 2007, cuando entró en vigor una normativa que limitaba ese metal por motivos de salud. El expresidente sostiene que las piezas son anteriores y de origen próximo oriental.

Los peritos añaden que resulta «incoherente» que joyas de ese valor carezcan de sus estuches originales y de la documentación de calidad e identidad que suele acompañarlas.

articles.headline: Police suspect dissident republicans sent the viable device to a Derry hotel
articles.subtitle: The package was delivered to The Ebrington hotel in the Waterside on Tuesday afternoon and destroyed in a controlled explosion; a local policing chair believes it may be linked to a Ministry of Defence stall at a careers fair there last month.
articles.body:
Police in Derry believe dissident republicans may be responsible for a viable postal device delivered to a hotel at Ebrington Square in the Waterside. The package was discovered at about 15:20 on Tuesday and Army Technical Officers carried out a controlled explosion before taking it away for forensic examination.

The Ebrington hotel was evacuated along with staff from neighbouring premises, and a Halloween funfair was running a short distance away at the time. Chief Superintendent Gillian Kearney condemned the attack as "shameful and utterly abhorrent", saying those responsible "clearly do not care who or what they harm".

She said the investigation was at an early stage and that police were keeping an open mind, with dissident republicans one line of enquiry. The chair of the local policing and community safety partnership said he believed the device may be linked to the Ministry of Defence having a stall at a careers fair held at the same hotel last month.

The Mayor of Derry and Strabane expressed solidarity with hotel staff and guests in the wake of what she called a traumatic alert, and the policing partnership condemned the delivery of the device during the city's Halloween festivities.

articles.headline: Israel's election leaves Netanyahu short of a majority as Arab-led parties surge
articles.subtitle: With 85% of ballots counted, Likud and its allies are on course for 53 seats against 48 for Eisenkot's bloc, while Arab-led parties are set for an unprecedented 19 — and almost no Jewish party will work with them.
articles.body:
Partial results from Israel's general election leave Benjamin Netanyahu leading his rival, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, but short of a majority in the 120-seat Knesset.

With 85% of ballots counted, Netanyahu's Likud and its far-right and ultra-Orthodox allies were on track for 53 seats. Eisenkot's Yashar party and three other Jewish opposition parties in his bloc were set for 48. Between 430,000 and 480,000 absentee ballots — from soldiers, diplomats and hospital patients — are still to be counted, so final results may take another day or two.

Arab-led parties are on course for an unprecedented 19 seats and could emerge as kingmakers, but all but one of the Jewish parties have pledged not to sit with them. Turnout was 77.7%, the highest in more than two decades; President Isaac Herzog called it "a badge of honour for Israeli society" and a sign of how deep the desire for democracy runs.

Both leaders say they will try to build a coalition. Once results are confirmed, Herzog will consult all the factions and invite whoever he believes has the best chance of succeeding, a process that could take weeks. If that fails, the country returns to the polls.

articles.headline: Flávio Bolsonaro, in Miami, calls himself 'the leader of Brazil' and denies fleeing
articles.subtitle: The senator declared himself the country's "true president" in a letter hours after landing in Florida, deleted it in the face of ridicule, and now insists it was never his intention to leave his homeland.
articles.body:
Brazilian senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who landed in Miami after losing Sunday's presidential run-off to Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, has said it was never his intention to "leave my homeland".

Hours after arriving on a private jet with his wife and two teenage daughters, the far-right senator published a letter declaring himself Brazil's "true president" — even though his own party and every Brazilian institution have recognised Lula's victory. The country's three main newspapers, Folha de S.Paulo, O Globo and O Estado de S.Paulo, described the claim as "coup-mongering". He deleted the letter and reissued it describing himself as "the leader of Brazil".

He had vanished for more than 24 hours after the result, reappearing when Argentina's migration service said he had entered the country by land on Tuesday night. From there he boarded a Gulfstream IV, reportedly routing through Ecuador to avoid Brazilian airspace, and walked out into a sunny Miami morning wearing a black bulletproof vest, met by no supporters and about two dozen journalists.

In the letter he thanked Argentina's president, Javier Milei, and Donald Trump for welcoming him, and repeated without evidence his claim of "electoral fraud", which Brazil's electoral court, supreme court and both chambers of congress have rejected.

articles.headline: Serbian police shoot dead a knife attacker outside the Israeli embassy in Belgrade
articles.subtitle: The interior minister says the assailant, a Serbian minor known to security services as an Islamic State supporter, rushed an officer shouting "Allahu Akbar"; Serbia has raised its terrorism threat level to red alert.
articles.body:
Serbian police shot dead a young man outside the Israeli embassy in Belgrade in the early hours of Wednesday after what the authorities called a "terrorist attack".

Interior minister Ivica Dacic said the attacker rushed at a police officer with two knives while shouting "Allahu Akbar". The officer suffered a minor knife wound to the face and shot him. The suspect has not been publicly identified, but Dacic said he was a minor and a Serbian citizen who had been monitored by security services as a "known supporter of the Islamic State"; they said he had posted an image of the Islamic State flag on Instagram.

Dacic raised the country's terrorism threat level to "red alert", the highest, meaning stricter security checks and more police at infrastructure sites and places where crowds gather. He visited the wounded officer, who was reported to be doing well and did not need hospital treatment. Israel's foreign ministry said no embassy personnel were hurt and the mission was closed at the time of the attack.

It is the second attack on the embassy in less than three years: in June 2024 a man shot a Serbian police officer in the neck with a crossbow and was killed by the wounded officer. Wednesday's attack came a day after Israel's election.

articles.headline: Putin courts African leaders in Moscow, casting Russia as the anti-colonial partner
articles.subtitle: The Kremlin is using the summit to widen a footprint built on security deals, grain and energy, presenting Russia as the continent's "best partner" rather than a colonial power.
articles.body:
Vladimir Putin is hosting African heads of state in Moscow, using the summit to present Russia as the continent's "best partner" and to draw a contrast with the former colonial powers.

The framing is deliberate. Moscow has rebuilt influence in Africa largely through security arrangements, grain supplies and energy projects, often with governments that Western capitals have distanced themselves from, and it is using gatherings like this one to convert those relationships into diplomatic weight.

The summit also serves a domestic purpose. With Russia under heavy sanctions and cut off from much Western finance and technology, African governments are among the few major buyers and partners still willing to sign deals publicly and appear alongside Putin.

The question analysts keep returning to is what, beyond arms and grain, Russia can actually deliver. Investment pledges have often outrun the money that arrives, and African governments increasingly weigh Russian offers against rival packages from China, the Gulf and the West.

articles.headline: Microsoft finally puts a dollar figure on Azure: $33.2bn in a single quarter
articles.subtitle: The disclosure lets investors compare Azure directly with AWS and Google Cloud for the first time; Azure came in slightly ahead of Google's $30.7bn and grew 48%, beating Microsoft's own guidance.
articles.body:
Microsoft has reported Azure's quarterly revenue in dollars for the first time, disclosing $33.2 billion for the quarter to the end of September. The company had previously shared only growth percentages or described revenue milestones in vague terms, making a like-for-like comparison with rivals impossible.

The figure puts Azure slightly ahead of Google Cloud's $30.7 billion in the same period, although Google's cloud unit — which also includes Workspace subscriptions — roughly doubled its revenue year on year, about twice Azure's growth rate. Amazon reports on Thursday, and AWS remains substantially larger.

Azure came in about $850 million above the $32.3 billion analysts had expected, and its 48% growth beat the 44% to 45% that chief financial officer Amy Hood forecast in July. It is now Microsoft's largest and fastest-growing product line, at roughly 36% of the group's $92.3 billion quarterly revenue.

Azure sits inside Agents and Infra, one of two new reporting segments that replace Microsoft's old three, grouping Azure with the Microsoft 365 cloud business; that segment brought in $76.8 billion, up 25%. A filing also showed Microsoft recorded $10 billion of revenue from OpenAI in the quarter — nearly 11% of total revenue — with $7.2 billion outstanding in receivables. Xbox hardware revenue fell 14%.

articles.headline: Apple's first touchscreen MacBook Pro starts at $2,899 and tops out at $14,549
articles.subtitle: The 14- and 16-inch Pros pair a 2,000-nit PROLED XDR touch display with M5 Pro or M5 Max chips and a hinge designed to stop the panel rocking when tapped; pre-orders open Friday.
articles.body:
Apple has launched a MacBook Pro with a touchscreen, the first time it has put touch on a laptop since the Touch Bar, which it later removed. The 14-inch model starts at $2,899 and the 16-inch at $3,399, and a fully specced 16-inch comes to $14,549 once memory and storage are maxed out.

The display is a new PROLED XDR panel rated at up to 2,000 nits of peak brightness in both HDR and SDR, with a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio and a Dynamic Island-style cutout in place of the notch. Buyers can choose between M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 16TB of storage.

Apple designed a hinge that stabilises the screen when it is touched, which also steadies the camera during video calls. The 14-inch weighs 1.38kg and the 16-inch 1.82kg, both lighter than their non-touch predecessors, with three Thunderbolt 5 ports, HDMI, an SDXC slot, MagSafe and a headphone jack.

Pre-orders open on 30 October and the machines ship from 6 November. Steve Jobs once dismissed touch on a laptop as "ergonomically terrible"; the launch is the second marquee product under new chief executive John Ternus, after the foldable iPhone Duo in September.

articles.headline: Records on 41,000 Homeland Security staff published after breach of its Okta login
articles.subtitle: Names, job titles, work emails, mobile numbers and office locations of CBP, ICE and CISA employees appeared online after a hacker claimed to have taken them from the department's single sign-on system.
articles.body:
Personal data belonging to more than 40,000 US Department of Homeland Security employees and contractors has been published online, after a hacker claimed to have taken it from an Okta single sign-on system used across the department's agencies.

The records include names, job titles, work email addresses, mobile numbers and office locations. More than half — about 21,000 — relate to Customs and Border Protection staff who work at airports and ports of entry. Around 10,000 belong to Immigration and Customs Enforcement and its Homeland Security Investigations unit, and just under 1,000 to the cybersecurity agency CISA.

The Okta system also holds IT and login records, including which systems each account can reach. The hacker, who uses the handle Department of Peace, left a note with the files saying: "They have our information, so it's only fair that we have theirs."

It is the second breach at Homeland Security this year, following the theft of personnel records from thousands of FBI agents and data on millions of serving and former military personnel from the Pentagon's human resources unit. Bluesky began blocking links to the leaked files after they circulated on the platform.

articles.headline: Google's AI spending is driving more searches — but AI Mode is still hard to monetise
articles.subtitle: Alphabet reported negative free cash flow of $9.07bn and $51.36bn of capital spending for the quarter, while it works out how to make AI-generated answers pay as growth in its core ad business slows.
articles.body:
Alphabet's quarterly results show a company spending heavily to defend its search business while still working out how to earn from the AI reshaping it. Google says its investments in AI are driving more searches, but its AI Mode answers remain difficult to turn into revenue, and the company is expanding AI search advertising globally as growth in its traditional ad business slows.

The group reported negative free cash flow of $9.07 billion and capital expenditure of $51.36 billion, below the $55.09 billion analysts expected, and kept its full-year capex forecast at $195 billion to $205 billion. It also said it still needs to rent compute from other providers to run parts of its cloud.

Google Cloud brought in $30.7 billion in the quarter, roughly double the year before and growing about twice as fast as Microsoft's Azure, which reported $33.2 billion. Both companies now disclose cloud revenue in dollars, making the comparison direct for the first time.

The results land as investors press every large technology company on whether the enormous sums going into data centres are producing returns. Alphabet's shares have swung on capex guidance all year, and the negative free cash flow figure is the clearest sign yet of how much of the search business's cash is being redirected into infrastructure.

articles.headline: Samsung's operating profit jumps 783% as AI memory demand outruns supply
articles.subtitle: The chipmaker reported operating profit of about 107 trillion won and revenue of 195 trillion won, the first time any technology company has cleared 100 trillion won in a single quarter.
articles.body:
Samsung Electronics has confirmed record quarterly results, with operating profit of 107.4 trillion won — about $80.5 billion — and revenue of 195 trillion won, roughly $146.3 billion. That is an increase of 783% and 127% respectively on the same quarter a year earlier, and the first time any technology company has reported quarterly operating profit above 100 trillion won.

The figures were first flagged in preliminary guidance on 7 October and are driven almost entirely by memory. AI data-centre demand for high-bandwidth memory, DRAM and NAND has tightened supply across the industry and pushed prices up, and the operating margin climbed to more than 50% from 14% a year earlier.

Samsung and Micron have both said they expect the gap between memory supply and demand to persist through 2028, and Samsung has warned that shortages will worsen in 2027. Analysts at KB Securities expect the most advanced HBM4 products to account for about 80% of Samsung's memory revenue next year, up from 40% this year.

The result underlines how completely the AI build-out has transferred pricing power from device makers to component suppliers. Rising memory costs are already feeding into PC and smartphone prices, and Apple's new MacBook Pro launch lands in the same week that flash memory pricing has become a board-level problem for hardware firms.

articles.headline: Google releases Gemini 4 Carbon, a frontier model most people will never get to use
articles.subtitle: DeepMind's second flagship in a fortnight leads cyber-defence benchmarks and is handed only to vetted security defenders through a programme called Fairwind, priced at $2 per million input tokens to begin with.
articles.body:
Google DeepMind has released Gemini 4 Carbon, its latest frontier model, two weeks after Argon. The company reports gains across the board and frames the launch mainly as a step forward in cybersecurity rather than a general upgrade for consumers and developers.

Most people will not get to try it. Carbon is being rolled out to selected cybersecurity defenders through a programme called Fairwind, at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, with pricing due to rise later to $4 and $20. Ars Technica's summary is blunt: Google has announced a frontier model you cannot use.

Gating a flagship behind vetted access reflects how labs now handle cyber-capable models. The same abilities that make a model useful for finding flaws in code can be aimed at real infrastructure, so access is restricted and monitored instead of published.

The cadence is as much the story as the model. Two flagship releases in a fortnight suggest DeepMind is shipping faster and in narrower slices, and that whatever benchmark lead it holds is measured in weeks rather than quarters. Google has not said when or whether Carbon's capabilities will reach its general models.

articles.headline: Nvidia's open speech model transcribes, translates and tells you who is talking
articles.subtitle: Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe handles 40 languages, attributes speakers in 13 and answers questions about a recording, in a 30-billion-parameter model that activates about 4 billion at a time and runs on one chip.
articles.body:
Nvidia has released Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, a free, open-weight speech model that follows text prompts and folds transcription, translation and speaker attribution into a single checkpoint.

It transcribes 40 languages, translates 31 of them to or from English and identifies speakers in 13, handling recordings up to an hour long with as many as eight speakers. The design is a mixture of experts with 30 billion parameters, of which roughly 4 billion are active per step, so it runs on a single chip — from the Jetson AGX Thor robotics board and the DGX Spark used in new laptops up to Blackwell data-centre systems.

Nvidia claims top placings on Hugging Face's Open ASR leaderboard for English among open-weight models, the lowest error rate on David AI's 21-language diarization leaderboard and first place in VoiceArena's 14-system comparison. It shipped alongside version 2 of Granary, Nvidia's open speech dataset, and fine-tuning recipes.

The appeal for anyone building meeting notes, call analytics or subtitles is that diarization and translation no longer need separate services, and the weights can run locally rather than being rented by the minute. It lands in a crowded month for voice models, with Mistral's Voxtral 3, ElevenLabs Realtime and Salesforce's Launa-Omni all arriving recently.

articles.headline: OpenAI lets US Pro users text their Dot agent over iMessage and RCS
articles.subtitle: The preview lets people send tasks, photos and voice notes to an always-on agent and get unprompted updates back in the same thread, without opening ChatGPT.
articles.body:
OpenAI has given its Dot agents a phone number, of sorts. ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US can now message a Dot through iMessage or RCS — the same channels they use for ordinary texting — and receive updates in the same thread.

Users can send text, photos and voice notes and hand over a task without opening the app. OpenAI says it partnered with Linq for messaging support and ran "extensive" penetration testing; only the account holder can text their Dot, and the Dot can only text them. Anything the agent writes to its memory is shared across its conversations.

Dots launched at DevDay on 29 September as always-on agents running on GPT-6 Astra, each with its own cloud computer and browser and connections to thousands of apps. Moving them into the default messaging inbox is a bid to make them part of everyday habit rather than a destination app people have to remember to open.

The feature is a preview, limited to Pro users in the US for now, and arrives as the personal-agent market heats up: Anthropic launched Claude Duet last week, and reviewers have found OpenAI's Dots the more polished of the two so far.

articles.headline: An Anthropic manager has stopped giving coding interviews, saying Claude does them better
articles.subtitle: Felix Rieseberg removed the coding test from his team's hiring loops this month, arguing it no longer predicts who will succeed now that AI writes most of the code; he is scouting portfolios for prototypes instead.
articles.body:
A hiring manager at Anthropic has dropped the coding interview from his team's recruitment, arguing that AI models now outperform candidates on the small challenges the test was built around.

"The coding interview is dead, at least for my team at Anthropic," Felix Rieseberg wrote. "I've seen enough to know that it no longer provides signal. I removed it from loops this month." In a blog post he said the old test now measures what the model can do rather than what the candidate will do in the job, and that he looks instead for small prototypes that show taste, empathy and principled thinking.

He also argued the shift creates an opening for junior engineers: "I'm seeing engineers who are comparatively new fly past people who are probably better coders and have been around much longer. Hunger beats tenure."

The change is one manager's call rather than company policy, and the wider market has not followed. ZipRecruiter's October survey of 1,500 employers found the information sector the most likely to require formal skills tests, at 62.5%. Google, by contrast, is expanding pilots of software-engineering interviews that let candidates use Gemini to test their AI fluency.
